_why: THE WIRE FORMAT FOR A SESSION ROW, pinned from both ends. The device serializes `TermSessionInfo` (agent/src/tools/terminal/mod.rs); the panel parses it in `useSessions`'s mappers (mapPending, mapGrants, mapPlan, mapGoal). Both parsers are DELIBERATELY defensive — a missing or mistyped field yields a default rather than an error, which is right for a live UI and means a renamed field would silently show nothing. So the format is pinned by a fixture read on BOTH sides: `agent/tests/fixtures/session-row.json` is asserted against the Rust serializer (a rename fails there) and fed through the panel's mappers (a parser that stops reading a field fails there). `last_exit_code` is the outcome of the last command the shell's own marker reported (round 96) — absent, not null, when nothing has finished with a code, so a surface can say FAILED without inventing it from output text; and `command_running` is the manager's own busy flag — the execute wait-loop sets it around the command it is waiting for — and it is on the row so the rail and every tab can say WORKING without inferring it from output recency (round 28 of the standing goal).

_notes.pending_approval: absent when nothing is waiting — the device omits it (skip_serializing_if), and mapPending returns null for a missing, null or id-less value
_notes.goal: absent or null when no objective is set; mapGoal trims and treats an empty string as no goal
_notes.expires_in_ms: a COUNTDOWN in milliseconds that SHRINKS on every read; the panel converts it once to an absolute deadline because a component that keeps the countdown while also accumulating time counts down twice as fast
_notes.idle_ms: silence since the last output, resize, write or break; drives the "nobody is using these" offer (an hour threshold)
_notes.last_exit_code: the exit code of the last command this session FINISHED, when the shell's marker reported one; ABSENT when no code was observed (no command yet, or the last wait ended without a marker — timeout, partial read, ssh/serial). CLEARED when a new command is written, so a stale code is never read as the new command's outcome.
